rules_boundary.engine_rules_basis: Official computer-competition rules explicitly based on world/former Asian rules, not domestic 2020.
rules_boundary.engine_cycle: Same piece placement and side-to-move on third occurrence ends game; cycle classification perpetual check=2, perpetual chase=1, allowed=0. Higher offender loses; equal grades draw. Perpetual chase requires a common target chased on every move and escaping on every reply; no check move anywhere in the cycle for chase definition.
rules_boundary.grounded_difference: Domestic 2020 clauses 24.10-24.13 include perpetual killing, chasing one OR multiple targets, and mixed check/kill/chase cycles as forbidden. Pikafish's published classification has only perpetual check, perpetual chase, allowed; these are not equivalent rule contracts.
rules_boundary.not_claimed: No exhaustive cycle-rule conformance corpus was executed. No domestic-2020 formal result is inferred from UCI score, bestmove, engine perft, or self-play termination. An independent formal adjudicator remains required for domestic-2020 application rules.

measurement_limits: All measurements are local Apple M1 Pro macOS arm64, not Cloudflare Containers or Workers.
One process with one search thread and 64MiB hash; no throughput/concurrency/load test.
Timing is wall-clock from Python perf_counter; startup includes process launch and configured NNUE readiness but is not an OS-cache-cold benchmark.
RSS snapshots from ps are instantaneous KiB, not total unique memory. Child ru_maxrss on macOS is bytes, includes child subprocess accounting, and is not a dedicated engine-only peak sampler.
Self-play move validation uses the same engine perft legal set, not an independent Xiangqi rules implementation.
30ms is a request, not a strict deadline: measured maximum self-play response was 59.688ms. Production must have external deadlines/cancellation/process recovery.
No browser UI, WASM build, remote execution, Cloudflare deployment, or domestic-2020 adjudication was performed.
